labels.text: Hand a task to a new cloud Code session for this GitHub checkout
Working on it in the cloud with

S60.01.needs: a signed-in AGI account and a GitHub checkout
S60.01.note: No separate work-task screen exists in the terminal. The normal message box starts an ordinary chat turn; agi code start is the only task-run entry found. The Code line's tui_app.rs references are a message send path, not a work-task composer.
steps: Run agi code --help and find the start line.
Run agi code start "Summarize the README in this folder" (add -y to skip the review prompt).
Read the review text shown before the cloud session starts.
Check the line 'Working on it in the cloud with' and the link it prints, then compare with Expected.
S60.01.where: agi code start "<task>" (type in a terminal), or agi code --help to see it

S60.02.note: This renames a chat session, not a separate work task. A cloud session with no title is listed as Untitled by agi code list.
steps: Start the agi chat screen.
Type /rename Quarterly report and press Enter.
Type /history and press Enter.
Check that the session shows the new title, compared with Expected.
S60.02.where: /rename <title> (typed in the chat), then /history to see the list

labels.text: What the cloud session should do.

S60.03.needs: a signed-in AGI account and a GitHub checkout
S60.03.note: The objective is the task text given to agi code start. No separate objective field was found in the local chat.
steps: Run agi code start "Fix the typo in docs/intro.md" -y and note the session id it prints.
Run agi code show <id>.
Check that the task text is shown back as what the session should do.
Compare with Expected.
S60.03.where: agi code start "<task>", then agi code show <id>

S60.05.note: The @ popup lists workspace files only. Connectors have a read-only policy screen at /connectors, and no per-task source picker was found, so the choice of connectors and project is partial.
steps: Start the agi chat screen.
Type @ in the message box.
Look at the popup and type a few letters of a file name to narrow it.
Check the list shows project files, compared with Expected.
S60.05.where: Type @ in the message box, then look at the list headed Files

labels.text: Tools the model can call in this session
Allow specific tools or tool patterns.

S60.06.note: Tools are chosen by a start flag only. No picker is shown before a run, so choosing per task is partial.
steps: Type /tools and press Enter.
Read the list titled Tools the model can call in this session.
Quit and start again with agi --allowedTools <names> using one tool name.
Type /tools again and check only that tool is listed, compared with Expected.
S60.06.where: /tools to view the tools; choose at start with agi --allowedTools <names>

S60.08.note: Whether the run record stores the chosen model was not confirmed in the code read.
steps: Type /model and press Enter.
Pick a model from the list.
Send a short message.
Compare the model shown in the status line with Expected.
S60.08.where: /model (typed in the chat), then pick a model

steps: Type /effort and press Enter.
Pick a level such as high from the list.
Check the message Effort set to ... and the effort: label in the status line.
Send a short message and compare with Expected.
S60.09.where: /effort (typed in the chat), then pick a level

labels.text: Each turn now stops once it has spent

S60.10.note: The cap applies to each turn, not to the whole task. The stop at the cap was not confirmed in the code read.
steps: Type /budget 5 and press Enter.
Check the reply Each turn now stops once it has spent 5 credits.
Send a task that costs more than the cap.
Check that the turn stops at the cap, compared with Expected.

labels.text: Plan approved. Mutating tools enabled for this session.
Plan rejected. Feedback queued for the model on the next turn.

S60.13.note: The terminal offers approve and reject, but no edit of the plan was found. A cloud work-plan review exists in apps/cli/src/cloud/work_plan.rs but no terminal screen for it was found.
steps: Type /plan and press Enter.
Send a task so the model writes a plan with update_plan.
Type /plan show and read the steps.
Type /plan accept, or /plan reject Use a smaller scope, and check the reply, compared with Expected.
S60.13.where: /plan to enter plan mode, then /plan show and /plan accept or /plan reject <feedback>

labels.text: No plan yet. Ask the model to call update_plan.

S60.14.note: Per-step status is produced by the plan's render_markdown, which was not read in full, so the accuracy of each step's status was not confirmed.
steps: Send a task that makes the model write a multi-step plan.
Type /plan show and press Enter.
Read the numbered steps shown under Plan.
Check the line with steps outstanding, compared with Expected.
S60.14.where: /plan show (typed in the chat) after the model writes a plan

labels.text: working, Esc or Ctrl-C to cancel

S60.16.note: The running state is shown per tool row (TranscriptCellState::Running). No separate current-step marker for a plan step was found.
steps: Send a task that uses several tools.
Watch the footer while it works.
Look for the tool rows in the transcript marked as running.
Compare the running row with Expected.
S60.16.where: Message box: send a task, then watch the transcript while it runs

S60.17.note: The line appears only when two or more tool or subagent rows are running together.
steps: Send a task that asks for several independent checks at once.
While it runs, look below the transcript for the line with the symbol and working at once.
Read the count and whether it says tools or subagents.
Compare with Expected.
S60.17.where: Send a task that makes the model run several tools or subagents at once, then look under the transcript

S60.18.note: The overlay appears only when the model chooses to call ask_user. The person cannot open it directly.
steps: Send a task such as: ask me which of two file names to use before you create anything.
Wait for the overlay titled Question from the agent.
Pick one choice, or choose Type your own answer and type a reply.
Check the agent continues with your answer, compared with Expected.
S60.18.where: Send a task that makes the agent call ask_user; the overlay Question from the agent opens

S60.19.needs: a test folder that you can delete
steps: Start agi --permission-mode approve in a test folder.
Send: create a file named test.txt that contains the word hi.
When the Tool Approval box opens, read the buttons.
Press No, then check that test.txt was not created, compared with Expected.
S60.19.where: Start with agi --permission-mode approve, send an action that changes a file, then the Tool Approval box opens

S60.20.note: Code shows queued prompts; it was not confirmed whether the queued text reaches the running turn or only the next one.
steps: Send a task that takes some time.
While it works, type new guidance and press Enter.
Check the footer says the message is queued.
Check the task is not restarted when the current turn finishes, compared with Expected.
S60.20.where: Message box: type a new message while the agent is still working, then press Enter

S60.22.note: This resumes a saved chat. Resuming a stopped step inside a running agent task was not found in the terminal code.
steps: Type /resume and press Enter.
Use the arrow keys to choose a session.
Press Enter to resume it.
Check that the earlier messages appear and the reply says Resumed session, compared with Expected.
S60.22.where: /resume (typed in the chat), then Enter on a session in the list

labels.text: working, Esc or Ctrl-C to cancel

S60.23.note: Server-side cancel is used only for a cloud turn started by agi code start (Ctrl-C prints Stopping the cloud turn). The local Esc path was not confirmed to cancel on the server.
steps: Send a task that takes some time.
While it works, look at the footer that says Esc or Ctrl-C to cancel.
Press Esc.
Check that the run stops and the transcript says it was stopped, compared with Expected.
S60.23.where: While the agent works, press Esc or Ctrl-C in the message box

S60.26.note: This copies the chat into a new session. It is not a copy of a work task's steps.
steps: Have a chat with a few messages.
Type /branch and press Enter.
Read the reply Branched conversation ... Resume with: agi --session <id>.
Open the new session and edit a message, compared with Expected.

S60.28.needs: a finished task in the chat
S60.28.note: The skill is written by the model from a prompt, so check the file content as well as its presence.
steps: Finish a short task in the chat.
Type /save-skill release-notes and press Enter.
Let the agent finish writing the skill.
Check that .agiworkforce/skills/release-notes/SKILL.md exists in the folder, compared with Expected.
S60.28.where: Type /save-skill <name> (typed in the chat) after a finished task

S60.29.note: No summary panel shown when a task ends was found. The final reply in the transcript is what the agent writes. /recap sends a prompt that asks the model for a recap. Searched for summary, result and recap in apps/cli/src.

S60.30.note: No list of files a task produced, with open or download, was found. /artifacts lists account artifacts and /diff shows workspace changes. Searched for deliverable, output file and artifact in apps/cli/src.

S60.32.needs: a signed-in AGI account with past cloud sessions
S60.32.note: /tasks lists only subagent tasks of this session. Cloud task history comes from agi code list.
steps: Run agi code list --status all.
Read each session with its state in brackets.
Run agi code show <id> for one session.
Compare with Expected. For local chats, type /history instead.
S60.32.where: agi code list --status all, then agi code show <id}

labels.text: Bring a cloud Code session here
Open a cloud Code session in the browser.

S60.34.needs: two devices signed in to the same AGI account, and a GitHub checkout on the second device
S60.34.note: Needs a second device to check, so it cannot be done on one machine alone.
steps: Start a cloud task on one device with agi code start "<task>".
On a second device, run agi code list.
Run agi code open <id> to follow it in the browser, or agi resume --teleport <id> in the same checkout.
Compare the state on both devices with Expected.
S60.34.where: agi code list, then agi resume --teleport <id> in a GitHub checkout, or agi code open <id> in the browser
